plan.topic: Possible plague exposure? What health authorities do next: identify close contacts, monitor them, give preventive antibiotics, isolate anyone with symptoms
plan.angle: 35–50 s. Open: 'Think you might have been exposed to plague? Contact a doctor or local health authority urgently. Don't self-treat or stockpile antibiotics.' Then 4 steps: health authorities trace close contacts, monitor them (CDC wording), give preventive antibiotics to close contacts where they decide it's needed, and isolate and treat anyone with symptoms. Status line: 'Irkutsk: plague suspected in media reports, not confirmed. Russian authorities report pneumonia of unknown cause; Rospotrebnadzor says over 90% of 197 contacts have finished monitoring (as of Oct 7, 2026).' Close: 'If you're worried, talk to a health professional.'

plan.why: Spin-off of L1: the contact-tracing playbook in 45 seconds, pointing to the Madagascar long-form. Action-framed titles got 57 for us, and the contact count is the most concrete fact in the story. | fact-check: Good action Short that fits the playbook. Fix the status line: Russian authorities officially call this pneumonia of unknown cause, and WHO says on Oct 8 that the cause is not yet known. 'Suspected, not confirmed' is fine only if the Short also says officials haven't confirmed plague and are reporting no dangerous pathogens in contacts. Credit the 197 contacts and 'over 90% monitored' to Rospotrebnadzor (as reported), dated Oct 7, 2026, and re-check before publishing. Step 3 must say health authorities decide on and give preventive antibiotics to close contacts, so it can't read as 'contacts should take antibiotics'. Take the incubation and monitoring wording from a reachable CDC plague page and quote it word for word. cdc.gov/plague/faq/ returned 404, so link the specific live page.

package.description:
Possible plague exposure? Health authorities trace close contacts, monitor them, decide who needs preventive antibiotics, and isolate anyone with symptoms. Status as of Oct 8, 2026: Russian authorities told WHO no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk and none was found among close contacts; WHO says the cause of death isn't officially confirmed. Not confirmed isn't ruled out.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. If you might have been exposed, contact a doctor or local health authority urgently. If you're worried, talk to a health professional.

Possible plague exposure? Here's what health authorities actually do next.

Step 1: Trace everyone who had close contact.
Step 2: Monitor them for fever, cough, shortness of breath and chest pain.
Step 3: Health authorities decide who needs preventive antibiotics — and give them. It's not a do-it-yourself plan.
Step 4: Anyone who develops symptoms is isolated and treated, and starting early matters.

Save this so you know how health authorities respond to a possible plague exposure.

WHO says her cause of death isn't officially confirmed. Not confirmed isn't ruled out. WHO rates the risk moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, and very low for the wider WHO European Region.

script.hook_pattern: Opens with a direct 'you' stake and the urgent action first: contact a doctor or local health authority urgently, and don't self-treat. Next comes a dated status check that says who said what. Media reports call it suspected plague. Russian health authorities told WHO no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk. WHO says the cause of death is not officially confirmed and gives its exact three-level risk rating (as of Oct 8, 2026). A WHO-attributed contact update follows (as of Oct 6, 2026). Then a 4-step numbered playbook, with a re-hook before step 3. It ends with a soft CTA to the L1 Madagascar video and the safety line.

factcheck.summary: The science and safety framing hold up. The WHO fact sheet backs the incubation figure ("can be as short as 24 hours"), monitoring of close contacts, the 7-day chemoprophylaxis, isolation and early curative antibiotics. CDC backs the four pneumonic symptoms and post-exposure prophylaxis, and the Madagascar 2017 report describes contact tracing, preventive antibiotics and isolation. The UN News WHO statement (Oct 6, 2026) matches s3 and s4 almost word for word. One major problem: s2 says Russian authorities told WHO that no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk. Neither the UN News article nor WHO's UN Geneva newsroom page says that. NBC News is the source, and it credits the statement to Russia's health watchdog directly. s2 also says no plague was found among her close contacts, but NBC says only 60% of contacts had been tested. Smaller issues: the myth/fact layout labels the media report as a "myth", which implies plague has been ruled out. WHO's Oct 6 statements are tagged "as of Oct 8". One s4 clause leaves out "among the contacts". The narration is about 216 words, close to the 90 s limit. The patient's name is not used. Re-check WHO and Rospotrebnadzor right before publishing.

issues.claim: Russian health authorities told WHO no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk, and none was found among her close contacts.
issues.problem: Wrong attribution. WHO's Oct 6 statement (UN News; Christian Lindmeier on the UN Geneva newsroom) does not say this. NBC News credits 'no case of plague has been recorded in Irkutsk' to Russia's health watchdog, with no mention of WHO. NBC also says only 60% of identified contacts had been tested, so 'none was found among her close contacts' goes further than the source.
issues.fix: Narration: "As of October 8, 2026, a lab worker's death in Irkutsk, Russia, is reported as suspected plague. Russia's health watchdog said no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk, NBC News reported on October 6. With 60% of her contacts tested, no plague was found." visual.fact: "Russia's health watchdog (NBC News, Oct 6, 2026): no plague case recorded in Irkutsk; none found in 60% of contacts tested". In hook_pattern, replace "Russian health authorities told WHO no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk" with "Russia's health watchdog said no plague case has been recorded in Irkutsk (NBC News)".

issues.problem: Calling the media report a 'myth' suggests plague has been ruled out. The status is suspected and not confirmed, and not confirmed isn't the same as ruled out.
issues.fix: Change visual.kind to "list" with items: ["Reported: suspected plague (media)", "Russia's watchdog: no plague case recorded in Irkutsk", "Not confirmed isn't ruled out", "As of Oct 8, 2026"]. Or keep the two-panel layout but rename the labels to "Reported" / "Official", not myth/fact.

hold_reason: Dropped by Editor-in-Chief: The rendered Short is 1.7 minutes (about 102 s), which is over the 90 s hard limit. The major fact-check problem is also still there. Every caption says "Russian authorities told WHO" that no plague case was recorded and that none was found among close contacts, but NBC credits that statement directly to Russia's health watchdog and reports that only 60% of contacts had been tested.

notes: Frame is just a lone newspaper icon on a plain gradient with a small label chip — violates the 'no lone icon on plain gradient' rule and doesn't reach ~25% hero coverage.

Caption at 31.1s reads 'HAS BEEN OFFICIALLY CONFIRMED.' with no visible 'NOT' — this directly reverses the on-screen title ('WHO: cause not confirmed') and the channel's core status-discipline rule. As shown, a viewer glancing at the caption alone would read it as plague being confirmed, which is false and against guardrails.

If 'NOT' exists in an intermediate frame not sampled, it's still risky: a critical negation word must never be the only word that scrolls off a caption line or appears in a frame the audience might pause on.
Caption 'NOT CONFIRMED ISN'T' is an orphaned fragment that reads as an incomplete/confusing claim on its own (should read something like 'not confirmed isn't ruled out').
Caption 'ONE THAT GETS MISREAD.' is an orphaned fragment that's confusing without the preceding clause visible in this sheet.
Composition is a lone pill mascot with scattered question marks on a plain orange gradient — reads as sparse.

audio.soundNotes: Overall music level is already close to target, nudged down slightly (0.95x) so pause level sits nearer -14 dB instead of -13 dB per the window. Trimmed a handful of loud outlier cues that broke the -14/-20dB speech-SFX ceiling (notably the swooshes at 12.4s and 61.3s), and thinned three busy clusters (24.6s bubble-swarm, 32.5-33.5s blip run, 71.5-71.9s blip pair, 82.3-82.8s transition pile-up, and the "Cause NOT confirmed"/"Not confirmed ≠ ruled out" serious beats) by dropping redundant hits so the sober clarifying lines stay clean. Added five bespoke textures at key story beats (open, status label, 24-hour stat, Madagascar example, closing reassurance) to give the science-channel polish without ever covering the narration.
